question.worked_solution:
We apply the power rule with $n=2$, and we get

$$
\int x^2 \,\textrm d x = \dfrac{x^{2+1}}{2+1} + C = \dfrac{x^3}{3}+C.
$$

Let's check by differentiating:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}+C) & = \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{{x}^{3}}{3})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(C) & = \\ \frac{1}{3}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{3})+0 & = \\ \frac{1}{3}\cdot 3{x}^{2} & = \\ {x}^{2}\,✓\end{aligned}
$$
